The hidden cost of manual forming and taping

Forming, testing and taping by hand is a bottleneck wearing a disguise

Before radial components can feed an insertion line, their leads must be formed, tested and packed into tape. Done by hand, that chain leaks quality, time and yield.

Forming by hand is inconsistent

Lead pitch and bend accuracy vary operator to operator — the insertion line downstream pays for every deviation.

Testing and sorting is manual

Capacitance and resistance values checked by hand are slow and error-prone; defective chips slip into good reels.

Taping speed caps the line

A manual taping bench cannot keep pace with an automatic insertion machine — the reel runs out and the line stops.

Clamping damage

Hand-held and clamp-fed components get scratched or bent before they are ever placed.

Maintenance eats uptime

Clutch-driven machines fail mechanically, and every breakdown is lost production and a repair bill.

No yield record

Without integrated testing and sorting, there is no per-lot yield data to improve against.

Installation guide

From delivery to production in five steps

Installation and operator training are included free with the S-300B.

01 · Layout

Place the machine (2200×1200×1500 mm, 700–900 kg) on a level floor with clearance for reel output and upstream feeding.

02 · Utilities

Connect 220 V / 50 Hz mains (1.6 kW) and compressed air at 4–5 kg/cm². No special foundation required.

03 · Tooling setup

Mount the fixture set for your product range (Φ4–Φ6 or Φ8–Φ10), set hole pitch (12.7 mm standard) and formed lead pitch.

04 · Test & trial

If configured with the tester, verify capacitance/resistance thresholds and sorting; run sample parts and check tape quality at full speed.

05 · Training & ramp

Free installation and operator training; 24/7 worldwide support and 1-day spare-part lead time.

Technical evaluation FAQ

Questions buyers ask before ordering

What does the S-300B do?

It forms the leads of radial-lead components (LEDs, capacitors, resistors), optionally tests their capacitance/resistance values, sorts good and defective parts, and tapes them into carrier tape — at 180 ± 20 parts per minute, in box or reel packaging.

Which products can it process?

Components with diameters of Φ6–Φ10 mm (conventional range Φ4–Φ10 mm). Φ4–Φ6 share one fixture set and Φ8–Φ10 share another. Product length is 5–30 mm and taping height 17–21 mm.

What pitches are available?

Hole pitch is 12.7 mm standard with a 4.1 mm hole diameter; formed lead pitch is 2.5, 3.5 and 5.0 mm standard, with 7.5, 10, 15 mm and other pitches available on request.

How does the testing function work?

When configured with the corresponding tester, the machine quickly measures the capacitance and resistance of each chip and automatically sorts good from defective products during the taping pass — defective chips never enter the reel.

What utilities does it need?

220 V / 50 Hz mains at 1.6 kW and compressed air at 4–5 kg/cm². The machine is 2200×1200×1500 mm and 700–900 kg.

How do I get a quote and configuration?

Email info@smthelp.com or WhatsApp +86 136 0256 2576 with your component drawings, product range and monthly volume. Configuration, quotation and a process recommendation are provided within 24 hours.
